subject.title: [Feature]: Add tools.web.fetch.allowPrivateNetwork to allow private network access

question: Should OpenClaw expose broad private-network access for arbitrary `web_fetch` URLs, and should the public contract be a nested/per-agent `ssrfPolicy.dangerouslyAllowPrivateNetwork` style policy rather than the requested top-level key?
rationale: The implementation primitive exists, but exposing it changes a security boundary and repository policy requires maintainer intent for new config/default surfaces and SSRF behavior.

options.title: Adopt nested/per-agent SSRF policy
options.body: Land a default-off `ssrfPolicy`-based contract, preferably scoped per agent, with audit warnings, docs, cache separation, redirect coverage, and metadata/link-local tests.

options.title: Accept a global broad opt-in
options.body: Expose one global private-network toggle and document that operators own the larger blast radius and migration contract.

options.title: Reject broad private access
options.body: Keep arbitrary `web_fetch` strict and direct users to trusted proxies, existing narrow fake-IP flags, or dedicated tools for internal services.

recommendation.title: Adopt nested/per-agent SSRF policy
recommendation.body: Land a default-off `ssrfPolicy`-based contract, preferably scoped per agent, with audit warnings, docs, cache separation, redirect coverage, and metadata/link-local tests.

likelyOwner.reason: This handle has the clearest maintainer-context comment on the unresolved policy and recent merged SSRF/web_fetch history.
